page: Microsoft Azure D48ns_v6 is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes 260 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across multiple domains. The CPU achieves a Passmark CPU score of 61,185.71 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 45,827.31, reflecting robust parallel processing capabilities. Memory performance is highlighted by a strong uncached read bandwidth of 253.44 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 105.32 GB/sec. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to strong cryptographic and vector processing speeds, as evidenced by a Passmark encryption score of 48,159.03. Additionally, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds of 336.16 tokens/sec for small language models (135M) and strong prompt processing capabilities.

From a resource density perspective, the D48ns_v6 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring substantial CPU compute and network throughput without the overhead of local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on external premium storage options. The server is highly suited for network-intensive applications, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
